newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania prosecutor urges jail for ex-communists.
newsitem.headline: Albania prosecutor urges jail for ex-communists.

text.p: A Tirana prosecutor on Tuesday demanded jail terms of up to 25 years for nine senior figures of Albania's former communist government charged with political persecution while in office, Radio Tirana said.
State prosecutor Shkelqim Gani called on Tirana's district court to convict the defendants for sending dissidents into internal exile.
One of the defendants, Llambi Gegprifti, used to be head of the communist party in the capital, Tirana, before the Stalinist dictatorship was toppled during protests in 1990.
Six others were senior members of the former Sigurimi secret police.

Around 100,000 Albanians were believed to have been forced into exile in remote villages during 45 years of communist rule, accused of expressing opinions against the Stalinist government or for trying to escape from the isolated state.
Three senior ex-communists were sentenced to death in May but an appeals court later revoked the sentences and imposed jail terms instead.
Thirteen others out of a total of 36 ex-communists indicted for crimes against humanity have been sentenced to between 16 and 25 years in jail.

No date has yet been set for the trial of former president Ramiz Alia, who succeeded hardline communist ruler Enver Hoxha, and two other former ministers, who are charged with ordering the shooting of Albanians who tried to flee the country.
